title: What if your toast always landed butter-side down? (15 s pipeline smoke test, not for posting)
formula: Scaled for 15 s: Hook -> Snap (impact) -> 'You see,' real-world turn -> punchline callback. Time markers, deadpan double and mystery beat dropped for length.
facts: Toast falling off a normal-height table only has time for about half a turn, so it usually lands butter-side down (R. A. J. Matthews, 'Tumbling toast, Murphy's Law and the fundamental constants', Eur. J. Phys. 16 (1995) 172, doi:10.1088/0143-0807/16/4/005).
A table about 10 feet (3 m) tall would give it time for a full turn and a butter-side-up landing (Matthews 1995, as summarised by Wikipedia 'Buttered toast phenomenon').

lines.narration: Your toast lands butter-side down. Not bad luck, *physics*.
lines.spoken: Your toast lands butter-side down. Not bad luck, physics.
lines.scene: Cold open on a sunny café terrace: a slice of buttered toast hangs mid-tumble, butter-side down, above the paving. You walk in behind it carrying an empty plate, neutral lidded face.
lines.camera: S1: over-the-shoulder ('you' shot), slow push-in toward the toast

lines.narration: Your table's too short for a full *somersault*... *Splat*.
lines.spoken: Your table's too short for a full somersault... [gasps] SPLAT.
lines.scene: The toast tumbles off the café table, half a turn, and slaps butter-down on the paving. Your face snaps to shocked on 'Splat'. Your friend at the next table holds up a judge's score card reading '½'.
lines.camera: S2: lateral truck along the table edge following the fall; one small impact kick on 'Splat'
lines.gag: Friend scores the toast's half-somersault with a '½' judge card

lines.narration: You see, from 10 feet up, it lands butter-side *up*.
lines.spoken: You see, from ten feet up, it lands butter-side up.
lines.scene: A fresh slice drops from high up and completes a full flip, landing butter-side up.
lines.camera: S3 start: crane up following the toast's path in reverse, revealing the height

lines.narration: So you buy a 10-foot table. Your friend needs a *ladder*.
lines.spoken: So you buy a ten-foot table. [laughs] Your friend needs a ladder.
lines.scene: Reveal: you sit at a comically tall café table, smug, toast butter-up on your plate. Your friend climbs a ladder against the table leg.
lines.camera: S3 continued: crane rises into a slow orbit around the tall table
lines.gag: The 10-foot café table, friend on a ladder
lines.expressions: you: smug on 'table'; friend: worried on 'ladder'
